notes: All counts run on the NFC-normalised text (String.prototype.normalize('NFC')).

code_points platforms (linkedin, linkedin_comment, instagram, facebook): count = number of Unicode code points. URLs and emoji count literally. These rules are assumptions (spec 11.1) until the template author verifies them against the real composers.

x (twitter-text v3): URL ranges are weighted first. In the remaining text, each emoji entity recognized by the pinned twemoji-parser 13.1.0 regex weighs emoji_weight (2). Invalid flag pairs, arbitrary ZWJ combinations, and selectors or joiners outside a recognized entity use the per-code-point rule. Every other code point weighs 1 in the configured inclusive ranges and default_weight (2) otherwise. Over = weighted count > limit.

URL rule (x only): extraction follows twitter-text 3.1.0 weighting needs. A scheme URL still requires a recognized domain. The pinned Apache-2.0 TLD table in twitter-text-v3-data.js includes gTLDs, ccTLDs, Unicode TLDs, and punycode. URL starts reject mention, hashtag, dollar, e-mail, filename, and adjacent-domain contexts. Paths and queries stop at twitter-text-compatible boundaries; balanced path parentheses stay in the URL, while unmatched punctuation and text after a t.co slug do not. Each extracted URL weighs url_weight (23).

Hashtags (instagram): a run of one or more '#' followed by a letter, mark, digit or '_' (\p{L}\p{M}\p{N}_), where the run is not preceded by a letter, mark, digit, '_' or '&'. Each match is one hashtag ('##tag' counts once, 'a#b' and '# x' count zero). over = count > limit OR hashtags > hashtag_limit.

fold (linkedin 210, instagram 125) is a visual hint only: after that many code points the preview shows the platform's own muted inline "… more" label (never inside a grapheme) and greys the rest, which stays readable. It never blocks anything.
linkedin_comment is the LinkedIn first comment (spec 4.7 first_comment, max 1250).
